subject: hvac
intro: HVAC leads to the climate-control trades: the technicians who install and diagnose refrigeration and heating systems, the sheet metal workers who build the ductwork, and the boiler crews and stationary engineers who keep big plants running.

roles.title: Heating, Air Conditioning, and Refrigeration Mechanics and Installers
roles.what: Install, maintain and repair heating, air conditioning and refrigeration systems: diagnose faults, test electrical circuits and components, charge refrigerant lines and replace worn parts on residential and commercial equipment.
roles.where: The refrigeration cycle unit — components, the pressure-temperature relationship, charging and diagnostics — plus thermodynamics, psychrometrics and EPA Section 608 certification are the working core of this job.

roles.title: Sheet Metal Workers
roles.what: Fabricate, assemble and install sheet metal products, most importantly the duct systems that move conditioned air through buildings, shaping and joining metal and sealing joints so systems perform as designed.
roles.where: The duct design and airflow measurement topics in the air distribution unit teach why duct geometry matters, and balancing systems explains what happens when the seams and fittings are not right.

roles.title: Boilermakers
roles.what: Assemble, install and repair boilers and other large vessels that hold liquids and gases: read blueprints, fit heavy plate and pipe, weld seams, and test vessels for leaks and pressure integrity.
roles.where: The heating systems unit's boilers and hydronics topic covers how boiler plants work, and the gas and refrigerant safety training maps to the pressure-vessel discipline the job demands.

roles.title: Stationary Engineers and Boiler Operators
roles.what: Operate and maintain the stationary equipment of large buildings and plants — boilers, chillers, pumps and generators — monitoring gauges and controls, performing preventive maintenance and keeping utility systems within safe limits.
roles.where: Boilers and hydronics from the heating unit and the refrigeration cycle's chiller side are the machines you would operate, while thermodynamics and heat transfer underpin keeping them efficient.
